descEn: Six-digit verification input

promptEn: Build an OTP verification screen with Tailwind CSS. Centered card explaining a 6-digit code was sent to an email. Show six separate square inputs (size-12, text-center, large font) in a row, an active-state focus ring, a "Verify" button, and a muted line "Didn't get it? Resend in 0:30". Q What did the week look like before?

Two spreadsheets and a man called Dennis. Dennis knew which depots could absorb a late lorry and which would quietly fail, and none of that was written down anywhere. When Dennis was on holiday we simply did worse.

Q Was there a moment it stopped being tolerable?

A Tuesday in January. Four depots reported the same pallet, so we sent three trucks to collect one thing. It cost about eleven thousand euros and nobody had done anything wrong — the system just let it happen.

The point was never the dashboard. It was that a planner on their second week can now make the call Dennis would have made.

Q How did the rollout actually go?

Faster than anyone predicted, which made me suspicious. We started with six depots for a fortnight, then did the remaining fifty-six over three weeks. The training was a forty-minute call and a one-page sheet.

Q What changed in the numbers?

On-time drops went from sixty-one to eighty-six percent, and duplicate collections effectively stopped. The one I care about most is that overtime fell, because the planners stopped firefighting at five o'clock.

Help centre

The answers people ask support for most often, grouped by where they live in the product.

Browse by topic

Billing 6 Accounts 4 Security 7 Data 3

Still stuck?

Send us the workspace name and we will look at the logs with you.

Contact support

Billing

When does the trial actually start?

On your first successful build, not on signup — so a workspace you set up and forget about does not burn the fortnight.

Can I switch from monthly to annual mid-term?

Yes. We credit the unused part of the month against the annual invoice, and the new term starts the day you switch.

Who can see invoices?

Owners and anyone with the Billing role. Add a finance contact under Settings → Billing and they will get the PDF without a seat.

Accounts

How do I transfer ownership?

The current owner promotes another admin and confirms by email. Transfers are logged and reversible for 24 hours.

Do inactive members still count as seats?

Only if they signed in during the billing period. Everyone else drops off the invoice automatically.

Security

Where are secrets stored?

Encrypted per workspace and decrypted inside the runner at build time. They never appear in logs, and the UI shows only the last four characters.

Can I require SSO for everyone?

Yes — enforce it per domain, and existing password sessions are ended the next time they refresh a token.

Data

How long are build logs kept?

30 days on Team, 12 months on Business, and you can stream them to your own bucket from day one.

Is there an export API?

Everything the dashboard shows is available as JSON. See the export endpoints in the API reference.

On the day you first add a payment method, not the day you signed up. If you upgrade mid-cycle we charge the prorated difference immediately and reset the renewal date to match.

Engineers on the product team, on rotation, 07:00–20:00 UTC on weekdays. Median first reply last quarter was 41 minutes. Sev-1 incidents are covered around the clock.

In the region you choose when the workspace is created — Frankfurt, Oregon or Sydney. Data does not leave that region, including backups and logs.

The workspace goes read-only at the end of the paid period and stays that way for 60 days, so exports still work. After that it is deleted, including backups, within a further 30 days.

Frequently asked

Seven answers, no marketing copy.

0 of 7 open
Do you have a free tier? Yes, and it is not a two-week trial in disguise.

The free plan is permanent and covers one workspace, three seats and 10,000 events a month. No card, and no countdown in the corner.

Which warehouses do you support? Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks and Postgres.

Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks and plain Postgres, plus anything that speaks the Postgres wire protocol. ClickHouse is in beta.

How fresh is the data? Five minutes by default, down to thirty seconds.

Scheduled syncs run every five minutes on all paid plans. Streaming sources land in under thirty seconds, and every chart shows the age of the data it is drawn from.

Can I self-host? On Enterprise, in your own Kubernetes cluster.

Enterprise customers can run the whole stack in their own cluster with a Helm chart we maintain. Updates are your call, though we ask that you stay within two minor versions.

What counts as an event? One row written or one API call — never both.

A single row ingested, or a single API request, whichever produced it. We do not double-count a row that arrives through the API, and retries are free.

Do you train models on our data? No, and it is written into the contract.

No. Customer data is never used to train shared models, and the DPA says so in a sentence your legal team can point at.

What is the uptime commitment? 99.9% on Scale, 99.95% with service credits on Enterprise.

99.9% on Scale and 99.95% on Enterprise, both measured monthly with credits applied automatically rather than on request.

Glossary

9 terms, written for people who did not build the thing.

E F G H I J–Z

A

Aggregation also called roll-up

Combining many rows into one figure — a sum, a count, an average. Every chart you see is an aggregation of something.

See also cardinality, dimension

Audit log

An append-only record of who did what and when. Nothing in it can be edited, including by us.

B

Backfill

Loading historical data into a new column or table after the fact, usually slowly and usually at night.

See also incremental sync

Burst capacity also called headroom

Short-lived allowance above your plan limit, so a launch day does not start returning errors.

C

Cardinality

How many distinct values a column holds. High cardinality makes charts unreadable and queries expensive.

Cursor

The marker a sync stores so the next run knows where it stopped. Usually an indexed timestamp.

Cache key

The fingerprint that decides whether two queries count as identical. Ours includes your access rules, so nobody sees a neighbour cached result.

D

Dimension

A column you group by rather than measure — region, plan, channel. Metrics are the numbers; dimensions are the slices.

Deprovisioning

Removing someone access automatically when your identity provider says they have left.

No term matches that. Ask support and we will add it.

Orders placed before 15:00 on a working day leave the same afternoon.

Delivery

Can I change the address after ordering?

Until the parcel is scanned by the carrier, yes — reply to the confirmation email. After that the carrier can usually redirect it for you.

Do you deliver on Saturdays?

In the Netherlands and Belgium, yes, at no extra charge. Elsewhere it depends on the carrier and is never guaranteed.

What about customs and duties?

Outside the EU, duties are payable by you on arrival. We declare the true value; we will not mark an order as a gift.

My parcel has not moved for a week

Write to us rather than the carrier. After seven days without a scan we send a replacement and chase the claim ourselves.

Returns

How do I send something back?
  1. Open the returns portal and enter your order number.
  2. Print the label, or show the QR code at a pickup point.
  3. We refund within three working days of it arriving.
Can I return something I have used?

Yes. Knives can be sharpened, pans can be seasoned. If it is genuinely worn out rather than unwanted, talk to us about repair instead.

What about a faulty item?

Send a photo and we replace it the same day, no return needed for anything under €40. Our guarantee runs for ten years on steel.

Do you refund the original delivery cost?

On a full return, yes, at the standard rate. On a partial return we keep the delivery charge, since the parcel still travelled.

Sixty days to change your mind, and we pay for the label within the EU. No restocking fee, and no need to explain yourself.

Common questions

If the answer here does not fit your case, the docs go considerably deeper.

How do I rotate an API key without downtime?

Create the second key first, deploy it, then revoke the old one. Both work simultaneously, so there is no window where requests fail.

Revoking takes effect within five seconds across every region — there is no grace period.

Why does my export have fewer rows than the dashboard?

Exports apply your row-level access rules, dashboards apply the report owner rules. If they differ, the export is the one telling the truth about your permissions.

Can I run two syncs against the same table?

Yes, provided they use different cursors. Two syncs sharing a cursor will leapfrog each other and both will miss rows.

What happens to scheduled reports when someone leaves?

They keep running under the workspace service identity, and ownership transfers to the workspace admin. Recipients are untouched.

Reports scoped to that person row-level rules will return fewer rows after the transfer. Check them.

Is there a sandbox I can break?

Every workspace has a staging environment on the same plan with its own keys and its own data. Break it as often as you like.

How long do you keep deleted data?

Soft-deleted for 30 days so you can undo, then removed from backups within a further 30. After that we genuinely cannot get it back.

Engineering

What we learned running our own build cache for two years

SM

Sam Mercer

17 August 2026 · 9 min read

We built the cache because the alternative cost more than an engineer. Two years on, it has paid for itself twice — and taught us three things we would rather have known on day one.

The cold start problem is a people problem

A cold cache is not slow because of the network. It is slow because nobody agrees on what a cache key should contain, so every team quietly adds one more variable until the hit rate collapses.

We fixed it by making the key a reviewed artefact: one file, one owner, and a test that fails when the key changes without a note explaining why.

A cache with a 40% hit rate is not a cache. It is a tax with extra steps.

Eviction beats capacity

For a year we answered every slowdown by adding storage. The fix was the opposite: evict aggressively, keep the index small enough to stay in memory, and accept a few extra misses on old branches.

cache.evict({ olderThan: "14d", keep: "main,release/*" })

Measure misses, not hits

Hit rate is a vanity metric — it goes up when builds repeat, which is exactly when nobody is waiting. What matters is the time a miss costs on the critical path, per branch, at the moment somebody is watching the pipeline.

Was it worth building?

For us, yes — but only because the cache is boring now. If you are still tuning yours every month, the honest answer is that you are running a small distributed systems project on the side of your actual work.

The cost of a column

MO Mira Osei·26 June 2026·9 min read

Adding a column is the cheapest thing you can do in a schema migration and the most expensive thing you can do to a system. The statement takes milliseconds. Everything after it takes months.1

Start with storage. A nullable timestamp on a table of four hundred million rows costs roughly three gigabytes once you account for alignment padding, and another three in every replica. That is not the expensive part.

The expensive part is that the column now exists in seven years of backups, in the analytics mirror nobody remembers configuring, and in the export somebody built for the finance team in 2023.2 Removing it later requires finding all of them.

A column is not a field. It is a promise to keep something working for as long as the table exists.

None of this is an argument against adding columns. It is an argument for knowing what you are signing, and for writing the removal plan at the same time as the migration.

If your table is over a hundred million rows, do not add a default in the same statement. Postgres has rewritten the whole table for less.

Footnotes

  1. 1Measured across eleven migrations at three companies between 2021 and 2025. The median time from "add column" to "column fully removed" was 19 months. ↩
  2. 2Finance exports are the single most common reason a deprecated column cannot be dropped. Ask before you assume nobody reads it. ↩
  3. 3The alignment maths differs by engine; the shape of the argument does not. ↩

1 Nineteen months is the median lifetime of a column that everyone agreed was temporary.

2 We keep a register of every downstream consumer per table. It is tedious and it has saved us twice. The template is public.

3 Alignment padding means a one-byte boolean rarely costs one byte.

Case study

Sixty-two depots on one plan, in a fortnight

How Kestrel Logistics replaced two spreadsheets and a very knowledgeable colleague with something the whole planning team could use.

+41%

On-time drops

14 days

To full rollout

−18%

Overtime hours

The situation

Kestrel moved 4,000 pallets a day across sixty-two depots, planned in two spreadsheets that only one person fully understood. When he was on holiday, on-time performance fell by eleven points, every year, predictably.

The failure that finally forced the issue cost eleven thousand euros in one afternoon: four depots reported the same pallet and three trucks were sent to collect it. Nobody had made a mistake.

What we did

We started with the six depots that complained loudest rather than the six that were easiest, on the theory that anything surviving them would survive the rest.

  • Modelled depot capacity from two years of historical loads
  • Replaced the overnight spreadsheet export with a live source
  • Wrote one page of training, tested on a new starter
  • Left the spreadsheets running in parallel for three weeks

The parallel run mattered more than anything else. It let the planners check the new numbers against instinct until instinct stopped disagreeing.

What changed

Duplicate collections effectively stopped. On-time drops rose from 61% to 86% within two months and have held there since. Overtime fell, because the five o'clock scramble largely disappeared.

The measure Priya cares about is different: a planner in their second week now makes the call that used to require six years of experience.
